name: Data Model Layer
description: Defines the logical data model: object schemas and their properties, enumerations, validation rules and the relationships between entities, independent of any particular storage technology (JSON Schema Draft 7). Entity classes, ORM models, interfaces, DTO and record types, and other type definitions that declare the shape of data are evidence for elements here; how that data is persisted belongs to the data-store layer. Modelling rules: data-model elements are passive structure; they are realized, accessed, referenced and mapped, and never serve, trigger or perform behaviour. A subschema written in place is part of what declares it (composes): a schema document composes its root schema and the definitions declared in it, an object schema composes its properties, an array schema its inline item schema, a composition its inline branches, and a property the value constraints it carries. A type declared elsewhere and reached by $ref or by name is referenced (references): a property references the object schema or definition its value takes, an array or composition references a named definition, and a Reference references the definition, object schema or document it points at. Subtyping is specializes. A declaration that only states a shape is an object schema, whether or not the shape is persisted or published: an interface or object type alias, a record, struct or dataclass of named, typed fields, an entity class or ORM model whatever the framework. A domain object (a class or object whose methods validate, derive from or change its own fields), or data handled with no declared shape, is an application data object, which an object schema may realize; that link is what tells data held to a declared shape from data that is not. A declared shape that is a published occurrence is an application event, one that is sent to a receiver is a message, and one that is an entry written to a log is an apm log record. Object schemas and definitions realize the application data objects and business objects they give form to (a direct link to the business object is a shortcut through the data object), an object schema realizes the message whose shape it declares, and schemas map to their counterparts in other layers (maps-to): API schemas, request bodies, responses and parameters, and data-store collections. Behaviour reaches data by accessing it: application functions, processes, interactions, events, services and components access object schemas, and functions, components and events access definitions, and business behaviour accesses the business objects they realize; a schema does not reference the behaviour that uses it. Schemas satisfy the requirements and constraints that govern the data but do not realize goals. The model is independent of technology: it does not depend on system software or use technology services, and the file that holds a schema document maps to a technology artifact.
